transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that for the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always moving. I'm constantly puttering around the house, fixing things, arranging this and that, or volunteering for just one more thing. You would think at 87 I'd be slowing down, but... I just have a really hard time just sitting down and being still.
When you're moving around and staying active like this, do your thoughts feel like they're racing or jumping from one thing to another?

No, not really. I wouldn't say my thoughts are racing. My mind feels pretty calm, actually. It's really just my body that wants to keep going. I just see things that need to be done around the house, and I get up and do them. But my head isn't spinning or jumping from one thought to another.
When you feel the urge to get up and move around or do things, does it feel like something you have to do to relieve anxiety or discomfort, or does it just feel like a natural desire to stay active?

No, I don't think it's anxiety. I don't feel nervous or uncomfortable, really. I just... well, it just feels like a natural desire to stay busy. If I'm sitting in my chair for too long, I just get the urge to stand up and find something to do. It's not because I'm worried about anything, I just prefer to be on the move.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory, balance, or coordination over this past year, or have you had any falls or difficulty with movements?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My memory seems about as good as it ever was, really. And I haven't had any falls or trouble with my balance. Like I said, I'm moving around just fine—probably too much! But my coordination is good, I'm not clumsy or anything. I just can't seem to stay put.
Have you had any medical conditions diagnosed recently, or has your doctor mentioned anything about changes in your brain or nervous system as you've gotten older?

No, nothing like that. My doctor hasn't mentioned any new conditions or anything about my brain or nervous system changing. I go in for my regular checkups, and everything always comes back fine. I'm pretty healthy, all things considered. Just can't seem to sit still.

When you have this urge to keep moving and stay busy, does it feel like there's an internal restlessness or discomfort inside your body that gets better when you move around, or is it purely just a preference to be active?

Well, I suppose it is a bit of an internal restlessness. When I'm at the senior center meetings or, you know, sitting through the long announcements at church, I get this sort of ants-in-my-chair feeling. I just have to shift around, or maybe stand up to get a cup of coffee, or even just straighten up the papers in front of me just to get through it. So yes, moving around does help that restless feeling.
When you get that ants-in-your-chair feeling, is it mainly in your legs, or is the restlessness more spread throughout your whole body?

It's not really just in my legs, no. It's more of an all-over feeling. I just feel like my whole body needs to be doing something, not necessarily just my legs needing to walk. It's just a general feeling of needing to be on the go.
Is this restless feeling and urge to move worse at certain times of day, particularly in the evening or at night when you're trying to rest?

No, I wouldn't say it's worse in the evening or at night. It's really just whenever I'm expected to sit still for too long, no matter what time of day it is. If I'm sitting in the afternoon, I feel it. If I'm sitting in the morning, I feel it. It doesn't seem to be tied to the time on the clock, just to what I'm doing—or not doing, I suppose. At night, once I finally get myself to lay down and go to sleep, I'm usually okay.

When you get that restless feeling, do you notice any particular sensations in your legs themselves—like tingling, crawling, or burning feelings—or is it more of a general urge to move your whole body?

No, I don't get any kind of tingling or crawling feelings in my legs at all. It's really just that general urge to move my whole body, like I mentioned before. I don't feel any burning or strange sensations like that, just the need to be doing something.
